result.summary: Clarke has quoted £198.37 + VAT (£238.04 if VAT is 20%) for the lounge spotlights and ceiling board. The only landlord approval on file is a system note with no amount, logged before any quote existed. So I emailed the landlord the quote and asked them to reply APPROVE or DECLINE. I also told Clarke the quote is with the landlord and asked him not to book any work yet. A hold is set to chase the landlord in 2 days.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 001/005 was a request for a quote, not an instruction to do the work. The approval in event 002 (approval id 7) was logged automatically 5 seconds after the ticket was created. It has no amount and came before the quote. No spend limit is recorded for the landlord, so the £198.37 + VAT quote in event 008 isn't clearly covered. Committing that money without the landlord seeing the figure would break the rule against spending a landlord's money without approval. Event 007 asked whether the provider needs a reply: yes, a short note to say the quote has been received and work shouldn't start yet.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the event 002 approval as cover and tell Clarke to go ahead
alternatives_considered.why_not: That approval has no amount and came before the quote. With no spend limit on file, committing £238 would mean spending the landlord's money without approval.
Nothing conflicts or is disputed. Getting the landlord's approval is the normal next step, and I can do that myself.

alternatives_considered.option: Return to auto mode without replying to the provider
alternatives_considered.why_not: Clarke would have no update and might book the work before the landlord has approved it.
